proposed.sourceName: Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam al-Kawthari — Darul Iftaa, Leicester (in 'Alcohol: Its Kinds, Usage and Rulings', central-mosque.com)
proposed.paraphrase: Fatwa relied upon (mufta bihi) per Imam Muhammad and held across the four Sunni schools that all types of alcohol are unlawful (haram) and impure (najis) even in small quantities, so cautious/strict practice avoids added ethanol in food — including flavor ethanol carriers.

proposed.sourceName: MUIS (Islamic Religious Council of Singapore) — Fatwa on Ethanol in Food Flavorings
proposed.paraphrase: MUIS permits ethanol (natural or synthetic) as a flavoring solvent when not produced from prohibited products and within strict limits (<=0.5% in flavoring, <=0.1% in final product) — representing the permissive side of a genuinely contested question.
